Sole-authored survey by a condensed-matter physicist. It takes novelty (a property the parts lack) as the defining mark of emergence and sets it against twelve other characteristics in §2. The six "objective" ones are discontinuities, order, modification of parts, universality, diversity and mesoscale modularity. The six "subjective" ones are self-organisation, unpredictability, irreducibility, contextuality/downward causation, complexity and intra-stratum closure. Case studies from the Ising model to Schelling segregation and LLMs show that each can come apart from novelty: novelty without discontinuity (Kondo, Fermi liquids, spin ice), without unpredictability (BKT, spin ice), and with reduction (Butterfield). §22 sides with weak emergence and argues that strong-emergence claims from molecular structure are weak. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-124); worth reading as a hub reference and example catalogue on emergence from physics outward, with unusually concrete case studies and a sceptical physicist's §15 on molecular structure. | [LIT-156](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-156.md) v4 | An Emerging Dilemma for Reciprocal Causation | Hazelwood (2023), DOI-10.1017/psa.2023.124. Hazelwood defines RC as "the process of natural selection is both a cause and effect of processes such as niche construction" and EC as "natural selection is an emergent causal process". He argues they are incompatible. Emergence here is Wilson's synchronic dependence plus autonomy, cashed out as Pence's composition. If EC holds, niche construction partly composes selection, so the two fail Woodward's independent-fixability condition and cannot stand in a causal relation. If EC fails, selection is either non-causal (statisticalism) or individual-level, which is incoherent because relative fitness needs a population (Millstein, Sober). EES proponents should drop RC but can keep niche construction as a genuine cause of the evolutionary *product*. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-137.md)); worth reading as a tight, well-sourced argument that brings the reciprocal-causation debate into the composition, exclusion and interventionism literature. | [LIT-157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md) v3 | Reproducees, reproducers, and Darwinian individuals | Bourrat (2025), DOI-10.1007/s11229-024-04880-w. Bourrat builds a nested vocabulary. A reproducee is a B that comes after A, is caused by A, and is of A's relevant class. A reproducer is a reproducee with reproductive autonomy, meaning it can reproduce across a range of backgrounds. A Darwinian individual is a reproducer with high reproductive causal control, meaning heredity survives as the parent's description is made finer. On that vocabulary, genes of multicellular organisms are, like hearts, mere reproducees, but with high control. Material overlap is necessary for reproducers, which are whole life cycles, and unnecessary for reproducees, so Griesemer and Godfrey-Smith partly talk past each other. Both quantities get an information-theoretic recipe (conditional MI after Bertschinger et al. 2008 for autonomy; interventional MI across grains, Griffiths et al.'s INF, for control), and neither is computed. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md)); worth reading as the clearest statement of the reproduced/reproducing distinction and a tidy, well-scoped settlement of the material-overlap dispute. | [LIT-169](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-169.md) v2 | Defining the niche for niche construction: evolutionary and ecological niches | Trappes (2021), DOI-10.1007/s10539-021-09805-2. Trappes compares NCT's evolutionary niche with the ecological niche. The evolutionary niche is the sum of selection pressures on a population (Odling-Smee, Laland & Feldman 2003), read "externally" as the environmental factors that produce fitness differences. The ecological niche is the conditions that permit continued existence; for a population, mean absolute fitness ≥ 1. Even at their closest, against the realized population niche, the two differ in extension. Habitat degradation is in the evolutionary niche but not the ecological one, and commensalism and non-limiting resources are in the ecological niche but not the evolutionary one. So NCT's niche is not the "simple translation" of Hutchinson's niche its proponents claim, and the evolutionary significance of niche construction must be shown case by case rather than following from the definition. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-155.md)); worth reading as a short, clean conceptual analysis that turns "persistence versus fitness differences" into a precise wedge between two fields' uses of "niche"; its empirical cases are admittedly thin (the CO2 case is offered as "possible"), and it analyses only the 2003 book's niche concept. |

Four fail: (a) Fisher's significance-test logic, (b) control of unknown confounders, (d) that observational studies "exaggerate" effects, and (e) probabilistic causality. The fifth, (c) selection bias, is a "cast-iron argument", but it supports only taking allocation out of the clinicians' hands, and randomisation is one way to do that. What matters is balance on plausible confounders, a placebo or active control and blinding. Whether balance comes from randomising or from matching "seems epistemically unimportant", and historically controlled trials can give strong evidence for large effects. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-126.md)); worth reading as the fullest single statement of the philosophical case against the special epistemic standing of randomisation. It is clearly argued and well documented, and it explicitly concedes the selection-bias argument. It is a partisan position piece, and its defenders-of-randomisation opponents (Pocock, Elbourne, Papineau) are summarised, not engaged at length. |

The paper sets out an idealized three-stage sequence of interaction types, which it calls a "first and rough sketch" (§1). Stage 1 is coordination in *collections* (pairwise, "aggregative" interactions of co-located individuals). Stage 2 is cooperation in *conexuses* (a connected web of binary interactions whose benefits can still be counted per member). Stage 3 is collaboration in *communities*: heterogeneous multi-way interactions around a shared goal, in which generatively entrenched "core" interactions give organizational closure. Table 1 puts the transition to a new level of individuality between stages 2 and 3 only. The paper asserts, rather than argues, that this describes evolutionary transitions non-circularly and that individuality is a special case of collectivity. Its one argued conclusion is hedged: community-level inheritance "seem[s] likely to evolve in tandem" with community-level individuality (§3). | Proposed — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)); a short programmatic sketch, and the authors call it one. It is worth knowing as the compact statement of Griesemer's scaffolding, reproducer and generative-entrenchment view applied to human social transitions. Its headline claims (non-circularity; individuality as a special case of collectivity) appear only in the abstract. Two things would settle it: the model of community "reliability" and endogenization the authors promise in §2 ("We hope to explore such models in future work"), or an application of the 3Cs to a worked case, such as the companion Neolithic paper, that separates collection, conexus and community by measurable criteria. |

For a perceptron whose weights follow overdamped Langevin dynamics and whose predicted labels are fast two-state processes, the information learnt about fixed random labels is bounded by the weights' total entropy production: Σ_μ I(σ_T^μ:σ^μ) ≤ Σ_n [ΔS(ω_n) + ΔQ_n] (Eq. 16, k_B = T = 1). This defines a learning efficiency η ≤ 1. The cost side includes the change in the weights' own Shannon entropy, and in the paper's toy model η → 0.99 as the heat ΔQ → 0 (slow driving). For a system driven by a stochastic signal through a fixed Markov kernel, the average work dissipated as the signal steps x_t → x_{t+1} equals, in units of k_BT, the system's instantaneous nonpredictive information, I[s_t;x_t] − I[s_t;x_{t+1}] (Eq. 14). Summed over a protocol, this total "nostalgia" lower-bounds dissipation and excess work (Eq. 18), and it adds to Landauer's bound: −β⟨Q⟩ ≥ I_e + I_mem − I_pred (Eq. 21). The paper defines a *superselection rule*: a decomposition of Hilbert space into orthogonal subspaces A, B, C, … between which there are no spontaneous transitions *and* no measurable quantities with non-zero matrix elements. Relative phases across subspaces, and hence relative parities, are then unobservable. It proves such a rule between integer and half-integer angular momentum, from time reversal with U_AKU_AK = +1 and U_BKU_BK = −1. It *postulates*, without conclusive evidence, a charge superselection rule. The consequence is that "all Hermitean operators represent measurable quantities" must be abandoned. | Active — read in full 2026-09-29 ([NOTE-304](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-304.md)); worth reading as the origin of the superselection concept and its first argued instance (univalence). | [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md) v2 | Notes on Landauer's principle, reversible computation, and Maxwell's Demon | Bennett (2002), arXiv:physics/0210005. Bennett states Landauer's principle as a consequence of the Second Law. A logically irreversible step, meaning erasure or a *merge of control flow*, must export at least the lost entropy (k ln 2 per bit) to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom. That export need not take the form of heat (p. 1). Logically reversible operations, including copying onto a blank register and measurement, have no minimum cost. He calls "an intrinsic cost of order kT for every elementary act of information processing" a 20th-century "misconception" (pp. 5–6). Erasing random data can itself be thermodynamically reversible; the waste comes from applying a many-to-one operation to *known* data (pp. 1, 4). | Active — read in full 2026-09-29 ([NOTE-310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-310.md)); Worth reading as a short, first-hand statement, by the principle's main defender, of what Landauer's principle requires (logical irreversibility) and what it does not (any cost for acquiring, copying or evaluating information). On the Earman–Norton "unnecessary or insufficient" dilemma Bennett concedes the point "with some justice" (p. 5) and defends the principle only as pedagogy. |

A one-locus model in which an individual's genotype affects relatives' fitness. Weighting each effect by Wright's coefficient of relationship r gives "inclusive fitness", which tends to be maximized as classical fitness is. An action that costs the actor is favoured only if the benefit to a relative exceeds 1/r times the cost: more than two brothers, four half-brothers or eight first cousins (§5). The increase of mean inclusive fitness is proved only for giving traits; the model is not about morality. | Active — read in full 2026-10-02 ([NOTE-401](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-401.md)); worth reading as the source of inclusive fitness and of the rule the moral-psychology literature calls Hamilton's rule. It proves that mean inclusive fitness increases only for genes whose total effect on others is non-negative (giving traits); for harming traits it shows only that selection points uphill. When individuals can choose partners and have equal outside options, a split that gives one side less than it could get elsewhere is not stable, so partner choice selects for sharing the gains of cooperation in proportion to contribution.
